# Anthropic Messages API

The only path in [[farely]] by which content leaves the phone. Used for one job: classifying a screen
the on-device keyword classifier could not name. The gating that makes it optional is the subject of
[[opt-in-cloud-fallback]]; this page is the integration itself.

## Call shape

- `vision.ts` — `classifyScreen(capture, apiKey)`, `VISION_MODEL = "claude-opus-4-8"`,
  `max_tokens: 700`, header `anthropic-version: 2023-06-01`.
- **Strict-JSON classifier prompt.** The response is constrained to
  `class ∈ {offer, trip, idCheck, appUpdate, unknown}` and `action ∈ {freeze, note, map-control,
  none}` — a small closed vocabulary the caller can switch on, not free prose. The prompt also
  explicitly instructs the model to **never propose tapping accept**, mirroring
  [[never-automate-the-accept-tap]] at the model boundary rather than trusting downstream code to
  filter it out.
- Result carries `VisionResult.method: "cloud" | "on-device"`, so provenance survives into the UI.

## Three transports, one function

`CapacitorHttp` on the device (native HTTP, sidesteps WebView CORS), a `/anthropic` Vite dev proxy in
local development, and a direct `fetch` with `anthropic-dangerous-direct-browser-access` otherwise.
That header is the notable one: it exists because browser-side calls put the key in the browser. Here
the key is the **driver's own**, entered in Settings and persisted to `localStorage` in plaintext —
never committed, never bundled, and `.gitignore` excludes `.env*`, `*.pem`, `*.keystore`, `*.jks`. The
plaintext storage is a real residual risk and is **not stated as a limitation anywhere in the repo**.

## Cost control

Because it is billed per call, the gating is the design: no key ⇒ no call at all; only
`WINDOW_STATE_CHANGED` events; a novelty-keyword gate; ≥5 minutes between calls per platform; and an
early return whenever the coordinator is frozen. Every call is written to
[[on-device-black-box-diagnostics]] as a `vision` event, so spend is observable after the fact without
any server.
